criteria.description: A summarize module exposes a function that, given a source file's path, content, and content hash, returns a well-formed structured summary object with EXACTLY this shape: a 'bullets' field that is a list of length 2, 3, or 4 where every element is a non-empty string, and a 'symbols' field that is a list where every element is a non-empty string containing no newline character (one-line-each descriptions of the file's functions/classes). The key name for the function/class list is the single fixed name 'symbols'.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic pytest with the Anthropic model call mocked to return a representative RAW payload (the same wire format the module parses from the live API, per c1a): call the summarize function on a sample source file and assert the returned object has a 'bullets' list whose length is in {2,3,4} with all elements non-empty strings, and a 'symbols' list where each element is a non-empty string and '\n' not in the element.

criteria.description: The module PARSES the model's raw response payload into the structured summary and NORMALIZES/VALIDATES it so the c1 shape invariant holds even when the model returns imperfect output. The parsed wire format is pinned: the module extracts summary data from the model's text response as JSON with 'bullets' (list of strings) and 'symbols' (list of strings), and this extraction succeeds even when the JSON is wrapped in surrounding prose and/or markdown code fences (e.g. a ```json ... ``` block). Normalization: (a) if more than 4 bullets are returned, they are clamped to the first 4; (b) any 'symbols' entry containing newline character(s) is split into multiple single-line entries (or the newlines stripped), and empty entries are dropped, so no returned symbol contains '\n' and none is empty. Bullet floor: if fewer than 2 non-empty bullets remain after stripping, the module MUST either raise a clear parse error OR pad to a minimum of 2 by deriving the extra bullet(s) from the model's OWN returned content (e.g. from a returned symbol or from returned prose) — it MUST NOT pad with a fixed constant/placeholder string, and MUST NOT return a malformed object with <2 bullets.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic pytest: mock the model to return a raw text payload with imperfect content — e.g. 5 bullets, a bullet that is empty/whitespace, and a 'symbols' entry containing an embedded '\n' plus an empty symbol. Assert the parsed result has bullets length in {2,3,4} all non-empty, and every 'symbols' entry is non-empty with '\n' not in it (the embedded-newline symbol having been split/stripped). Include a case where the model wraps the JSON in a ```json ... ``` fence with leading/trailing prose and assert it still parses. Include a case where the model returns fewer than 2 usable bullets: assert the module either raises a clear parse error OR yields >=2 non-empty bullets AND that any padded bullet is NOT equal to a fixed placeholder constant (assert the padded bullet is derived from the model's returned symbols/prose, e.g. it is not one of {'(no summary)','.','N/A',''}).

criteria.description: Summaries are keyed by the file's content hash and looked up in the in-memory cache. Given a cache that already contains a VALID summary (per c4's validity definition) under a file's current content hash, the summarizer returns the cached summary WITHOUT invoking the model.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic pytest: pre-populate the cache dict with a valid summary under a file's content hash, run summarization with a mocked model client, and assert the model call mock was invoked zero times while the returned summary equals the cached one.

criteria.description: A changed content hash triggers re-summarization. When a file's content (and therefore its hash) differs from the cached entry, the summarizer invokes the model exactly once and stores the resulting summary keyed by the new hash. The stored summary is DERIVED FROM that model call's returned payload (not a stale/cached value) and conforms to the c1 shape (single-line 'symbols' entries, 2-4 'bullets').
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic pytest: cache a summary under an old hash, then summarize the same path with new content/new hash and a mocked model whose return payload contains a recognizable sentinel bullet/symbol; assert the model mock was called exactly once, the new summary is stored in the cache keyed by the new hash, the stored summary contains the mock's sentinel value (proving it derives from that call), and each 'symbols' entry contains no '\n' and bullets length is in {2,3,4}.

criteria.description: The cost cap is enforced deterministically against a single named cap constant defined in the module (e.g. CAP = 200). A cached summary is 'valid' iff it conforms to the c1 shape (bullets length in {2,3,4}, every bullet a non-empty string, every 'symbols' entry a non-empty string with no '\n'); a cache entry that fails this shape is NOT valid and does not count as covering a file. Only files classified as source count toward the cap. The cap triggers when source_count > CAP; the number of source files selected for summarization equals min(source_count, CAP). Selection is the largest files by line count, ties broken deterministically by path (line_count descending, then path ascending). Every source file that is neither selected-by-cap nor already covered by a valid cached summary carries an explicit 'unsummarized' marker in the output data and is NOT sent to the model. Cache×cap interaction is pinned and non-churning: a source file that ranks BELOW the cap but already has a VALID cached summary under its current content hash RETAINS that cached summary (it is NOT force-marked unsummarized and is NOT re-sent to the model); only below-cap source files with no valid cached summary are marked unsummarized.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic pytest with mocked model: import the module's cap constant; feed a synthetic all-source set of size CAP+50 (e.g. 250 when CAP=200) with varying line counts including some ties, run the summarization pass, and assert (a) the count newly summarized == min(source_count, CAP) == CAP, (b) the selected set equals the top files ordered by (line_count desc, path asc), (c) the model was invoked only for those selected files lacking a valid cached summary, and (d) every below-cap source file with no valid cached summary carries an explicit unsummarized flag/status. Add a case: 250 source files, cap 200, with ONE below-cap-ranked source file pre-populated in the cache under its current hash with a VALID summary → assert it retains its cached summary, is NOT marked unsummarized, and the model is NOT called for it. Add a case where a below-cap source file has a MALFORMED cache entry (e.g. bullets length 1, or a symbol containing '\n') under its current hash → assert that entry does NOT count as covered, so the file is marked unsummarized (and not silently returned as valid). Also assert that with source_count <= CAP no cap-trigger/unsummarized marking occurs.

criteria.description: A delta module exposes a function that takes a current scan (list/collection of per-file records with path, line_count, hash) and a previous snapshot's file records, and returns a structured delta result object (dict or dataclass) capturing per-file line-count changes and drift facts. It performs pure computation with no LLM, network, or filesystem dependency.
criteria.verifyBy: Hermetic pytest constructs in-memory current and previous file collections and asserts the returned delta structure has the documented top-level keys/fields (e.g. per-file deltas, growers, shrinkers, added, deleted, no_baseline) and correct types.

criteria.description: For a file present in both current and previous with a higher line count, the delta reports a positive per-file line-count delta equal to current_lines - previous_lines; for a lower line count it reports the corresponding negative delta. The per-file delta is line-count-based only: hash equality is NOT required for a zero delta.
criteria.verifyBy: pytest with a file grown from N to N+k asserts delta == +k, a file shrunk from N to N-k asserts delta == -k, and a file with same line count but different content hash asserts delta == 0.

criteria.description: Files present in the current scan but absent from the previous snapshot are reported as new/added files; files present in the previous snapshot but absent from the current scan are reported as deleted files. Matching is keyed by file path, and added/deleted entries carry their line counts.
criteria.verifyBy: pytest with a current-only path and a previous-only path asserts the added list contains the new path and the deleted list contains the removed path, each with its line count.

criteria.description: Biggest growers and biggest shrinkers are derived from per-file line-count deltas of files present in BOTH scans: growers are files with positive deltas ordered by magnitude (largest growth first), shrinkers are files with negative deltas ordered by magnitude (largest shrink first). Ordering is deterministic: primary key is delta magnitude descending, with a documented stable tie-break (by path ascending). Files whose line count is unchanged appear in neither growers nor shrinkers.
criteria.verifyBy: pytest supplies several files with mixed positive, negative, and zero deltas — including at least two files of equal delta magnitude — and asserts growers/shrinkers are the correct files in descending magnitude order with the documented path tie-break applied deterministically, and that unchanged files are excluded from both.

criteria.description: New/added files do NOT appear in growers and deleted files do NOT appear in shrinkers. Growers and shrinkers are drawn exclusively from files present in both the current and previous scans; additions and deletions are reported only in the added/deleted facts, never as growth or shrinkage.
criteria.verifyBy: pytest with one added file and one deleted file asserts the added path is absent from growers (and appears only in added) and the deleted path is absent from shrinkers (and appears only in deleted).

criteria.description: An unchanged file (same path, same line count, and same content hash across both scans) produces a zero line-count delta and is not classified as a grower, shrinker, added, or deleted file.
criteria.verifyBy: pytest with an identical file in both scans asserts its per-file delta is 0 and it is absent from growers, shrinkers, added, and deleted.

criteria.description: The first-run case (no previous snapshot: previous is None or absent) is signaled explicitly as a no-baseline condition (e.g. a boolean flag such as no_baseline=True or a distinct sentinel), rather than emitting a delta of all-zeros or treating every file as added.
criteria.verifyBy: pytest calls the delta function with no/None previous snapshot and asserts the result carries the documented no-baseline signal and does NOT populate growers/shrinkers/added/deleted with fabricated values.

criteria.description: The computed delta facts are integrated into the snapshot/data model the renderer consumes via a single, concretely named documented field on the run/data-model object, so a downstream renderer can read drift facts without recomputing them. For the baseline case that field is populated with the delta facts; for the first-run case it carries the no-baseline signal. If the snapshot JSON is the renderer's input, the field survives serialization round-trip.
criteria.verifyBy: pytest builds the run data model / snapshot object for a scan with a prior baseline and asserts the delta facts are accessible on the specific documented field name; a separate assertion builds the first-run structure and asserts the same field carries the no-baseline signal; if deltas are persisted, a round-trip through the snapshot serialization preserves the field.
